name: PlayDapp
rootCause: The blockchain gaming platform PlayDapp was hacked, with the attacker's address being added as a minter, minting 200 million PLA tokens (valued at $36.5 million). Shortly after the incident, PlayDapp sent a message to the attacker through on-chain transactions, requesting the return of the stolen funds and offering a $1 million bug bounty reward, but negotiations ultimately failed. PlayDapp's PLA token on Ethereum was compromised in February 2024 after an attacker obtained a privileged admin key, added themselves as a minter, and minted 1.79 billion PLA. Only about $32 million was converted; the rest was rendered worthless as exchanges froze tokens and migration excluded attacker-minted PLA. A privileged token contract admin key was compromised, allowing an unauthorized address to gain mint privileges and inflate the token supply without restriction, due to lack of multi-signature or timelock protection.
